methods.label: Recover the population ratios
methods.explanation:
A combined average weights each group by its number of students. We can recover these weights by balancing the total score deficit below an average against the total surplus above it.

At Adams, each boy's group average is \(74-71=3\) points below the school average, while each girl's group average is \(76-74=2\) points above it. Thus three times the number of boys equals twice the number of girls, giving
\[
\text{Adams boys} : \text{Adams girls}=2:3.
\]
At Baker, the corresponding deficit and surplus are \(84-81=3\) and \(90-84=6\). Hence
\[
\text{Baker boys} : \text{Baker girls}=6:3=2:1.
\]
Now use the combined boys' average of \(79\). Adams boys average \(8\) points below \(79\), and Baker boys average \(2\) points above it. Balancing their totals gives
\[
\text{Adams boys} : \text{Baker boys}=2:8=1:4.
\]
Together, these ratios make the four group sizes proportional to
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{Adams boys}&:2, &\text{Adams girls}&:3,\\
\text{Baker boys}&:8, &\text{Baker girls}&:4.
\end{aligned}
\]
These are relative weights; the common population factor cancels when computing an average. The girls' combined average is therefore
\[
\frac{3\cdot76+4\cdot90}{3+4}
=\frac{588}{7}
=\boxed{84},
\]
which is choice D.
